prompt: In “Compute Comes in Many Chassis,” match each illustrated height allocation to its compute example.

pairs.feedback: The compact compute example occupies 1U. Compute systems also come in other heights.

pairs.match: Dual-node chassis with two independent nodes
pairs.feedback: The 2U example contains two independent compute nodes. This is an illustrated chassis arrangement, not a universal rule.

pairs.match: Multi-node platform with shared chassis infrastructure
pairs.feedback: The 4U example shares chassis infrastructure across multiple compute nodes. Storage products may also use 4U, but they are a separate example.

feedback_correct: These matches describe the compute examples taught here. U measures height allocation; it does not prescribe workload, performance or a universal equipment role.
feedback_incorrect: Recall the three compute-chassis examples: compact, dual-node and shared multi-node. Avoid inferring a universal role from height alone.
